set.body:
VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. I ran introduction.Rmd's rsa() example against the package. Every coefficient on the only model RDM is negative:

       (Intercept) category
  [1,]       2.100   -1.288
  [2,]       2.100   -1.383
  [3,]       1.350   -0.467
  [4,]       1.433   -0.458
  [5,]       1.000   -0.133
  [6,]       0.525   -0.188

The vignette prints this at :150-151 and the next sentence, :154, is:

  'Named RDM axes are aligned to the geometry's effect identities.'

It says nothing about the sign. To anyone RSA-literate - which is the entire target audience - a uniformly negative model coefficient reads as 'the category model is ANTI-predictive of the neural geometry'. The package's flagship demonstration of its headline method shows the method rejecting the hypothesis, unremarked.

THIS IS NOT A CODE BUG. I checked why, and the arithmetic is correct and consistent:

  category_rdm (:143-149) encodes face and house as SAME category (0) and object as
  different (1). So the model predicts face-house should be the SMALLEST distance.

  The actual geometry, from rdm(g) on the same data:
       measurement face - house face - object house - object
          feature1     2.100000      1.400000      0.2250000
          feature2     2.100000      1.050000      0.3833333

  face-house is the LARGEST distance and house-object the smallest - exactly inverted
  from what the model RDM predicts. Hence a negative coefficient. The package is right.

The failure is that the hand-typed run1/run2 matrices at :48-57 were written without anyone checking whether they instantiate the category structure the RSA section then tests. The numbers were chosen to look plausible, not to encode a hypothesis. Everything downstream is arithmetically correct on data that contradicts the example's own premise.

WHY THIS IS DAMAGING OUT OF PROPORTION TO ITS SIZE. A reader evaluating this package runs the RSA example, sees negative coefficients, and reaches one of three conclusions, all bad: the package is broken, RSA here means something different from what they know, or they have misunderstood the setup. There is no fourth reading available to them, because the vignette offers no comment. The most likely outcome is that they close the vignette.

CONNECTION TO bd-01KZY8KX8R32RR4T6741XTJXKT: this is the strongest argument yet for a generator with KNOWN GROUND TRUTH. Hand-typed illustrative matrices cannot be checked against the hypotheses the docs later test on them, and this is what that failure looks like in practice. A generator that plants a category structure makes this class of error impossible - the example would recover what was planted, and the docs could say so.

TWO REPAIR OPTIONS, and I lean to the second:
  1. fix the toy data so face and house genuinely pattern together
  2. KEEP the negative result and TEACH it. This vignette already argues, at :126-127
     and :165-167, that negative estimates are meaningful and are deliberately not
     truncated. Here is a live negative estimate with a real interpretation sitting
     unused in the same document. Turning it into 'the category model is not supported
     in this data, and here is how you would know' would demonstrate the package's
     most distinctive scientific stance instead of asserting it in five places, which
     is exactly the missing vignette the reviewer identified.

Option 2 costs one paragraph, needs no data change, and converts the single worst-looking output in the docs into the best teaching moment in them.
set.title: The flagship RSA example demonstrates the model FAILING, and the vignette does not notice
